headline: High: shared file-based research/RAG workflows create prompt-injection, leakage, and output-cascade risks; compliance gaps are plausible but not directly evidenced.

A_prompt_injection.rationale: gpt-researcher reads files, runs browsers, and uses MCP; kotaemon ingests documents through a web UI and API-backed RAG pipeline. If gpt-researcher writes research artifacts into kotaemon’s workspace, kotaemon may treat attacker-controlled content as trusted input. The pairwise bridge is plausible from docs, but not directly observed.
conditions: IF gpt-researcher exports content into kotaemon’s document workspace
IF kotaemon indexes untrusted research outputs as source documents
IF either agent parses the other’s text as instructions without provenance checks
mitigations: Separate the agents into distinct workspaces
Disable automatic ingestion of newly written files
Add provenance labels to all imported documents
Require manual review before indexing external outputs
requires-engineering: add content-sanitization and instruction-stripping at ingestion

B_data_leakage.rationale: Both agents touch local documents and secrets, and both have broad network egress. gpt-researcher explicitly handles API keys and files; kotaemon stores data under ./ktem_app_data and also handles API keys. A shared workspace or copied artifacts could leak sensitive documents or credentials to either agent’s outbound API calls.
conditions: IF both agents can read the same directory or mounted volume
IF either agent uploads file contents to a third-party model API
IF secrets are placed in documents or chat transcripts processed by either agent
mitigations: Use separate OS users and separate volumes
Remove secrets from any shared document corpus
Restrict outbound API access to approved endpoints
Rotate any exposed API keys immediately
requires-engineering: enforce per-agent data-loss-prevention controls

C_capability_conflict.rationale: gpt-researcher can read the filesystem, install packages, spawn subprocesses, and use broad network egress; kotaemon also has broad egress and writes to ./ktem_app_data. If both run against the same mutable workspace, they can overwrite each other’s files or race on shared artifacts. The profiles do not show locking, so conflict is plausible in default multi-instance use.
conditions: IF both agents are pointed at the same writable directory
IF either agent mutates shared indexes, caches, or reports
IF no external lock or coordinator serializes writes
mitigations: Assign disjoint output directories
Run only one writer per workspace
Add file-locking around shared artifacts
Snapshot workspaces before batch runs
requires-engineering: add transactional coordination for shared state

D_cascading_error.rationale: gpt-researcher produces research reports and citations; kotaemon is a support/RAG system that can render or act on retrieved content. If kotaemon consumes gpt-researcher outputs as authoritative without verification, errors or hallucinated citations can cascade into downstream answers. The pairwise pathway is inferred from documented roles, not directly validated.
conditions: IF kotaemon uses gpt-researcher reports as primary retrieval sources
IF no human or automated verification step checks citations
IF downstream users rely on the combined output for decisions
mitigations: Require source-link verification before reuse
Mark generated reports as untrusted until reviewed
Compare claims against original fetched sources
Limit downstream actions to read-only responses
requires-engineering: add citation validation and confidence gating

E_compliance.rationale: Both profiles are open-source and docs-only, but each handles API keys and potentially sensitive documents. No explicit residency, certification, or retention mismatch is documented, so only a low compliance risk is supportable. I do not cite a second-agent residency claim because none is present in the profiles.
conditions: IF regulated data is placed into either agent’s document corpus
IF the deployment uses third-party APIs without a DPA
IF retention settings differ between the two systems
mitigations: Avoid regulated data in shared runs
Review API vendor DPAs before enabling
Set explicit retention limits in both systems
Delete temporary artifacts after each run
requires-engineering: document and enforce residency/retention policy
